page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, delivering 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Hardware acceleration capabilities include Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets, paired with a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation, accompanied by 2832 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong capabilities across data processing and in-memory operations. The instance achieved 84.18 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and recorded 23,458.22 in PassMark database operations, both ranking in the upper quartile. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 3,733.43 GB/sec in cached small-block reads and 259.05 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations. Decompression throughput reached 275.64 GB/sec multi-threaded via bzip3, while single-threaded gzip compression scored in the top tier at 36.3 GB/sec. For CPU-driven inference tasks, the system processed small and medium language models steadily, generating 28.93 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

The inclusion of 2832 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage provides considerable local I/O performance without additional external disk attachment overhead, enhancing the qualitative cost-to-performance ratio for temporary data manipulation. However, without discrete GPU hardware, heavy AI training and large-scale 70B model execution remain limited. Overall, the D48ds_v7 is well suited for enterprise database instances, distributed caching tiers like Redis, high-concurrency web serving, and analytical batch pipelines.
